headline: Two weeks on, 12,333 homes are affected and 3,129 destroyed, with 40,791 people in affected homes; the number of people in shelters has risen to 6,654 as unsafe homes are tagged red. A second death has been confirmed. Reconstruction of 43 m² earthquake-resistant homes is under way.
key_points: Official (Govt briefing 22 Oct): 2 deaths, 27 injured; 12,333 homes affected (40,791 residents), 3,129 with total damage; 6,654 people in 122 shelters (most in Veraguas); 576 schools; 23 bridges need rehabilitation.

Damage concentrated in Los Santos (5,060 homes evaluated) and Herrera (3,267); homes are tagged green, yellow or red, with a public map on panamaconecta.gob.pa. Livelihoods hit: ~2,400 dairy farmers in Azuero, rice harvest at risk.
Deaths: Elena Barría (68, Macaracas, 14 Oct) and Regina Miranda (60, Santiago, injured evacuating a school, 22 Oct).

Housing: 43 m² two-bedroom earthquake-resistant homes (46 m² accessible), about US$19,000–27,000 each; construction under way in Herrera, Coclé and Chiriquí; no rebuilding in risk zones; Teletón (24 Oct) aims to fund 2,700 homes.
Schools: 770 reopened in 12 regions on 21 Oct; Coclé students will finish the year with guides and modules; classes still suspended in Los Santos, Herrera and Veraguas.

Finance: US$310M credit and guarantee programme for small businesses (Banco Nacional, MEF, IDB); CCRIF payout US$17.4M; US$2.48M to local governments; US adds US$1M. Government says damage is 'far from' US$450M.
Science: surface rupture with ~1–1.2 m horizontal and ~1 m vertical offset at Búcaro; Isla Cañas sank 15–30 cm, flooding farmland.
Risks: heavy rain (green alert) on landslide-dammed areas; aftershocks continue at a declining rate; water shortages in Azuero.

areas.area: Los Santos (Macaracas, Tonosí, Las Tablas, Pedasí)
areas.text: Most homes evaluated of any province (5,060). Macaracas reports 1,000+ homes affected and the first death; Tonosí hospital replaced by tents and a modular unit, new hospital planned; Isla Cañas sank 15–30 cm and seawater flooded farmland; Búcaro shows ~1 m surface fault rupture. Colour-tagging of homes started here.

areas.area: Herrera (Los Pozos, Las Minas, Pesé, Ocú)
areas.text: 3,267 homes evaluated; 20 of the 35 collapsed schools are here (13 in Las Minas, 6 in Los Pozos); landslides and isolated communities in the hills. First reconstructed homes in Pesé and Las Minas; CSS clinic in Los Pozos working from tents.

Hosts most people in shelters (3,500+). Mariato: 17 schools lost, ~5 km of highway and several bridges damaged, weight limits on five Atalaya–Mariato bridges; Cañazas: 400+ homes affected; Montijo: 33+ homes uninhabitable; Santiago: second death (a school secretary injured during evacuation).

Penonomé cathedral tower and governorship building damaged (the latter may be demolished); Hotel Dos Continentes partly collapsed; homes lost in La Pintada (Agua Fría) and El Bajito de San Miguel. Students will finish the year with guides and modules.
Eastern Chiriquí (San Félix, Remedios, Tolé) and adjoining Ngäbe-Buglé communities: mostly adobe homes damaged; 139 schools affected; reconstruction started in San Félix.

Five floors of Hospital Santo Tomás's old maternity building evacuated; Policlínica Presidente Remón closed; other services back to normal (Metro, Tocumen, ports). Colón: Hospital San Juan and municipal market partly damaged.

services.text: 12,333 homes affected, 3,129 destroyed; 6,654 people in 122 shelters. Homes tagged green/yellow/red; construction of 43 m² homes started.
770 schools reopened in 12 regions on 21 Oct; classes still suspended in Los Santos, Herrera and Veraguas; Coclé finishes the year with guides and modules; 35 schools collapsed.
42–67 facilities damaged; US$61M for repairs; Tonosí hospital in tents and a modular unit; Santo Tomás old maternity building evacuated; mental-health line 800-6467.
Most roads reopened; 47 critical points and 23 bridges need rehabilitation; weight limits on five Atalaya–Mariato bridges; MOP repair costs due in early November.
Power restored, including Isla Cañas; water shortages persist in parts of Azuero.
Tocumen and Metro Lines 1 and 2 operating since 12 Oct; state ports back to ~80%.

upcoming: Coming up: Teletón 20-30 on Sat 24 Oct (target: 2,700 homes); road and bridge repair costs from MOP in early November; decision on classes in Los Santos, Herrera and Veraguas.
unknowns: Homes destroyed (only Chiriquí's 10 reported) and the final housing count — MIVIOT housing census under way.
When access, power and water will be restored to Tonosí and the Mariato coast.
Whether heavy rain triggers further landslides on damaged slopes and roads.
When schools will reopen and how many need structural repair.
Total cost of damage: the government has not published an estimate; road and bridge costs are due within two weeks and housing costs depend on the 10,000+ evaluations.
